summary: The incident is caused by the expiry of payment-service's outbound mTLS client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z (H1, confidence 0.86). The cert-watcher warned 25 minutes in advance (F11), the first hard failure occurred 27 seconds after notAfter (F12), and both bank_api_error_rate (100%) and payment_success_rate (2.51%) broke at exactly the 12:15Z bucket (F9, F10). Because failing bank calls were absorbed as PENDING_RETRY instead of HTTP 5xx, payment-service's aggregate HTTP error_rate stayed flat at ~0.22% (F8), which is why the dashboard looked green while customers saw ~97% transfer failures. Traffic volume was unchanged and latency dropped (fast failures, no restarts), excluding load, retry-storm, timeout-config, and shared-dependency mechanisms (F13 vs F2/F3). The exact TLS error side (peer rejecting our cert vs. our client rejecting the peer) and the absence of any renewal are asserted from caller-side logs only, which caps confidence at 0.86 but does not change the fix: reissue/renew and hot-reload the client certificate.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Expired mTLS client certificate causes bank-partner-api calls to fail (silent partial failure)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: payment-service's outbound client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expired at 12:15Z, so the mTLS handshake to bank-partner-api is rejected; failing transfers are absorbed as PENDING_RETRY instead of HTTP 5xx, keeping the error-rate panel green while customers see ~97% transfer failure.

causal_chain.claim: payment-service mTLS client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal reached notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z; cert-watcher warned 25 min early at 11:50:26Z
At exactly 12:15:27Z the first hard failure occurs: bank-partner-api rejects the mTLS handshake with 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'
payment-service absorbs the failed bank call as PENDING_RETRY rather than returning 5xx, so HTTP error_rate stays flat (~0.22%) and the dashboard stays green
bank_api_error_rate jumps from 0.20% to exactly 100.0% at the 12:15Z bucket; payment_success_rate collapses from ~99.25% to 2.51%
Customers experience failed fund transfers (~40 tickets); request volume and latency profile confirm fast failures at the bank-call step, not a load or client-side issue

assumptions: The client certificate was not renewed before/at expiry anywhere in the path (no evidence of renewal; cert-watcher only warned)
No other cause simultaneously broke the bank handshake — the dominant ERROR text is unambiguously the expired cert
PENDING_RETRY did not drain and complete later, i.e. transfers genuinely failed

ranked_hypotheses.title: bank-partner-api (external dependency) outage or policy change rejects payment-service calls
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The bank partner's API degraded or changed its TLS/trust policy around 12:15Z, so payment-service's calls fail at the handshake; the 100% bank_api_error_rate and 2.5% payment_success_rate reflect a partner-side failure rather than payment-service's own credential.

causal_chain.claim: bank-partner-api is an external dependency with no telemetry of its own; its health can only be inferred from caller-side signals
At 12:15Z payment-service bank_api_error_rate goes to 100% and success_rate collapses
Handshake failures were logged as mTLS rejections with a remote 'expired certificate' alert at 12:15:27Z

assumptions: The partner-side service, not our client cert, is what broke — despite the log explicitly naming OUR cert's notAfter=12:15:00Z
cert-watcher's expiry warning is coincidental to the onset

ranked_hypotheses.title: Timeout config change (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000) altered retry/absorption behavior on the bank path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 11:20Z payment-service config change 'bank.api.timeout_ms' 3000->5000ms changed how bank calls fail, converting bank-call problems into silently absorbed PENDING_RETRY rather than surfaced errors; combined with a partner advisory this produced the green-dashboard-but-failed-transfers symptom.

causal_chain.claim: payment-service key bank.api.timeout_ms changed 3000->5000ms at 11:20Z, described as raised after a partner advisory
The change is the nearest preceding change to the 12:00-12:30Z onset window (40+ min earlier)
Failed bank calls were absorbed as PENDING_RETRY instead of 5xx, hiding failures from the error-rate panel
This produces customer-visible transfer failures with a green dashboard

assumptions: Longer timeout changed failure classification — no log evidence shows timeouts; the dominant errors are TLS/mTLS rejections, not timeouts
The 40+ min gap between the change and onset is causally bridged

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared downstream (ledger-db or kafka) degradation causes transfers to fail silently
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared component on the payment path (ledger-db IOPS/disk, or kafka consumer/producer lag) degraded at onset, so transfers stop settling and only surface as customer tickets while payment-service HTTP errors stay green — echoing precedents HIST-110/HIST-111/HIST-114 or HIST-112/HIST-104.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db is marked shared:true and is read/written by order, portfolio, payment and settlement services; kafka is also shared

Historical precedents show slow/failing payment and settlement paths traced to ledger-db IOPS throttling, full-table scans and disk-full WAL, plus a settlement consumer stall after partition reassignment
Payment failures could accordingly be absorbed silently as PENDING_RETRY with no HTTP 5xx

assumptions: Shared-component degradation coincides exactly at 12:15Z — no ledger/kafka telemetry was retrieved (explicit gap)
ledger/kafka failures would not log as mTLS/TLS certificate errors (they do not)
Precedent-based plausibility substitutes for direct evidence, which is absent

ranked_hypotheses.title: Client-app/bank-side reporting artifact only; payment-service genuinely healthy
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 40 support tickets reflect a client-app or bank-side issue, and payment-service is healthy — the flat HTTP error_rate accurately represents service health.
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: client app / bank partner (external, not payment-service)

causal_chain.claim: HTTP error_rate stayed flat (~0.22%) across the whole window

assumptions: Aggregate HTTP error_rate alone is sufficient to declare payment-service healthy — contradicted by the collapse in payment_success_rate to 2.51%
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: payment_success_rate collapsed to ~2.5% (F10) and bank_api_error_rate hit 100% (F9) with 311 ERROR-level lines naming an expired client certificate (F12); payment-service is demonstrably failing at the bank-call step, not healthy.

facts.statement: payment-service HTTP error_rate remained flat/normal across 11:45-13:59Z (mean 0.22%, max 0.32%), explaining the green dashboard panel; this metric only counts HTTP 5xx returned to the caller, while failing bank calls were absorbed as PENDING_RETRY.
payment-service bank_api_error_rate jumped from a 0.20% baseline (11:45-12:09Z) to exactly 100.0% starting with the 12:15Z bucket and stayed at 100.0% through 13:57Z.
payment_service success rate collapsed from ~99.25% (12:09Z) to 2.51% (12:15Z) and remained ~2-2.8% through 13:57Z, matching the ~40 support tickets.

A cert-watcher WARN at 11:50:26Z flagged that the payment-service client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal was due to expire at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, 25 minutes before any customer impact.

The first hard failure was at 12:15:27Z when payment 45f233b6 was marked PENDING_RETRY after the mTLS handshake to bank-partner-api was rejected; dominant ERROR patterns are 'marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' (140 occurrences, first_seen 12:15:27Z) and 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' (171 occurrences, first_seen 12:16:44Z). 311 of 314 WARN+ERROR lines are ERROR-level.

payment-service request volume was steady (~100 req/s, 90.2-109.6; 12:15Z bucket 101.27) with no restarts, and p99 latency dropped from ~320ms to ~140ms at the 12:15Z boundary (fast failures rather than completed bank round-trips), ruling out traffic surge and client-retry storm.

Only one deployment occurred in any service between 09:00Z and 13:59Z on 2026-04-02 (settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30:00Z) and only one config change occurred across all services (payment-service 'bank.api.timeout_ms' 3000->5000 ms at 11:20:00Z); neither is timestamped inside the reported 12:00-12:30Z onset window.

payment-service's dependency map includes outbound edges to ledger-db (db, shared), bank-partner-api (external), and kafka (queue-produce, shared); bank-partner-api has no telemetry of its own (has_telemetry false).

Matched historical precedents involving payment-service or its shared components include HIST-105 (bank partner API outage), HIST-110/HIST-111 (ledger-db IOPS throttling and full table scans), HIST-114 (ledger-db disk full), HIST-109/HIST-115 (silent auth/pool failures), HIST-104/HIST-112 (kafka rebalance/consumer lag).

assumptions: The client certificate was not renewed before or at expiry anywhere in the path; no renewal evidence was found and the cert-watcher only warned.
No other cause simultaneously broke the bank handshake; the dominant ERROR text unambiguously names our expired client certificate.
PENDING_RETRY transactions did not later drain and complete, i.e. the transfers genuinely failed from the customer's perspective.

The exact TLS error side (the bank peer rejecting our expired client cert, versus our client rejecting the peer's certificate) is inferred from caller-side logs only and was not independently confirmed.

The two change-listing tools cover infra-level changes (volume/IOPS, broker maintenance, certificate renewal, gateway config); if they do not, a coincident infra change in 11:50-12:15Z could be invisible.
Absence of a recorded renewal is a true absence rather than a coverage limit of the change/config listing tools.

timeline.event: Only deployment in the window: settlement-service v1.9.0 (CSV exporter), status live, not rolled back.
Only config change in the window: payment-service 'bank.api.timeout_ms' 3000 -> 5000 ms by p.nair ('Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory').
payment-service HTTP error_rate begins a flat/normal run (mean 0.22%, max 0.32%) that continues to 13:59Z; bank_api_error_rate baseline 0.20% through 12:09Z.
Earliest anomaly: cert-watcher WARN that payment-service client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expires at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z (25-minute early warning).

Certificate notAfter reached. bank_api_error_rate jumps to exactly 100.0% and payment_service success rate collapses from ~99.25% to 2.51% at this bucket; request volume unchanged (~101 req/s) and p99 latency drops ~320ms -> ~140ms with no restarts.
First hard failure: payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY after the mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api was rejected.

ERROR log 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' first seen; 311 of 314 WARN+ERROR lines are ERROR-level.
Incident INC-005 [SEV-2] reported by support lead: ~40 customer tickets about failed fund transfers; payment-service error-rate panel green.
Last observed data: bank_api_error_rate still 100%, success rate still ~2%, HTTP error_rate still ~0.22% - failure persists unmitigated to the end of the window.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately renew/reissue and hot-reload the payment-service outbound mTLS client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal (or roll the payment-service pod/credential mount to load a valid cert), then confirm bank-partner-api calls succeed.
recommended_actions.rationale: The expired client cert is the identified root cause (H1): the cert hit notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, the first handshake rejection followed 27 seconds later, and bank_api_error_rate has been pinned at 100% with success rate ~2.5% ever since. Reloading a valid credential is the only change that can restore the bank leg.

recommended_actions.action: Replay/drain the PENDING_RETRY backlog for payments failed since 12:15Z and verify each transfer settles against the ledger, rather than attempting retries against the broken handshake.
recommended_actions.rationale: 'Drain vs genuinely failed' is an explicit assumption behind H1; the ~97% failed transfers absorbed as PENDING_RETRY must be reconciled so customers either get settled transfers or correct outcomes.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm the recovery objectively: watch bank_api_error_rate return to ~0.2% and payment_success_rate return to ~99% in the 12:15Z-style per-minute buckets, and confirm the 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' ERROR pattern stops.
recommended_actions.rationale: F9/F10 give the exact pre-incident baselines (0.20% bank error rate, ~99.25% success) and F12 the exact error signature; these are the acceptance criteria for a verified fix.

recommended_actions.action: Replace the cert-watcher's WARN-only behavior with an automated pre-expiry renewal/alerts that page an on-call owner when an mTLS client credential on the bank path will expire within a defined lead time, and add a hard-fail guard so an expired credential cannot silently degrade into PENDING_RETRY.
recommended_actions.rationale: F11 shows the system had a 25-minute warning it did not act on; the mechanism only stayed silent because bank-call failures were absorbed instead of surfaced.

recommended_actions.action: Add bank-leg health monitoring that alerts on bank_api_error_rate and payment_success_rate (per-partner where possible) instead of relying on the aggregate HTTP 5xx error_rate panel.
recommended_actions.rationale: F8 shows the aggregate error_rate metric is structurally blind to absorbed bank-call failures, which is the exact reason a SEV-2 customer-visible outage presented as a green dashboard.

recommended_actions.action: If the certificate reload does not restore the bank leg, pivot to discriminating observations: check whether a renewal or infra change occurred between 11:50Z and 12:15Z (coverage limit of the config/deployment tools per F1-F3), and obtain any bank-partner-side confirmation to distinguish an expired-cert rejection from a partner-side policy change (H2).
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 remains at 0.12 and bank-partner-api has no telemetry, so a residual alternative cannot be excluded by caller-side data alone; this action bounds that uncertainty.

data_gaps: No ledger-db, kafka or bank-partner-api telemetry was retrieved for 12:00-12:30Z, so a co-occurring shared-component degradation could not be directly excluded; bank-partner-api exposes no telemetry at all (F5), so its health can only be inferred from payment-service caller-side signals.

The change/config listing tools each returned only a single record and it is unknown whether they cover infra-level changes (volume/IOPS, broker maintenance, certificate renewal, gateway/envoy config), so absence of a 12:00-12:30Z change may be a tool coverage limit rather than a true absence.

No exact historical precedent for 'customer-reported payment failures while the HTTP error-rate dashboard was green' was found; closest matches (HIST-105, HIST-109, HIST-115) have match_score <= 2, so the mechanism is supported by analogy only.
Per-endpoint/per-partner/per-status-code error breakdowns and 4xx vs 5xx vs timeout splits were not obtainable, so it cannot be stated whether one bank partner or client segment was more affected.

Resource metrics (cpu_pct, memory_pct, db_pool_in_use, restarts) for payment-service and shared dependencies, plus queue depth / thread pool metrics, were never retrieved, so co-occurring resource saturation or an unbounded PENDING_RETRY backlog cannot be ruled out.
Logs for transfer/settlement/ledger components were not reviewed, so it is unconfirmed whether PENDING_RETRY transactions were drained, dropped, or accumulated downstream.
Observed metrics were unavailable: query_metrics(metric=error_rate, service=bank-partner-api) failed with not_found (tc-016), limiting independent partner-side verification.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Bank-partner-side confirmation that our client certificate was still trusted and that the partner itself changed TLS policy or trust store at ~12:15Z would move the conclusion toward H2 (partner-side failure) rather than our expired credential.

Evidence that the client certificate had actually been renewed before 12:15Z (or that a valid, newer cert was loaded and still rejected) would falsify H1 and implicate a partner-side or trust-chain cause.

Discovery of an infra or certificate-renewal change between 11:50:26Z and 12:15:00Z invisible to the current change-listing tools would open a mechanism competing with the expiry itself and lower confidence in H1.

Finding that failing bank calls were caused by timeouts or connection-pool exhaustion (rather than 'tls: expired certificate, alert 45') would support H3 or H4 and contradict the TLS-expiry mechanism.
ledger-db or kafka telemetry showing an outage, IOPS throttling, or consumer lag beginning at 12:15Z would raise H4 and challenge H1 as the origin of the customer-visible failure.

Evidence that the PENDING_RETRY backlog drained and the transfers eventually completed would invalidate the assumption that customers' transfers genuinely failed and lower severity/relevance of the root cause.

findings.statement: Only one deployment occurred in any service between 09:00Z and 13:59Z on 2026-04-02: settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30:00Z ('Batch settlement report export', 'new CSV exporter'), status live, not rolled back.

Only one config change occurred across all services in the window: payment-service key 'bank.api.timeout_ms' changed 3000 -> 5000 ms at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z by p.nair, described as 'Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory'.

Neither recorded change is timestamped inside the reported 12:00-12:30Z onset window; the nearest preceding change to that window is the payment-service timeout change at 11:20Z (40+ min before onset), and the settlement deployment is at 10:30Z.
payment-service dependency map: inbound from api-gateway (http); outbound edges payment-service -> ledger-db (kind db), -> bank-partner-api (kind external), -> kafka (kind queue-produce).

Shared components on the payment path: ledger-db is marked "shared": true and is written/read by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service; kafka is also shared. bank-partner-api is external with no telemetry (has_telemetry false).

Historical precedents involving payment-service or its shared components: HIST-105 'Payment failures: bank partner API outage' (2025-11-19, payment failures with bank api errors, dependency_failure); HIST-110 'Slow orders from ledger-db IOPS throttling' (2026-01-15, statement timeouts/slow queries, match_score 4); HIST-111 'Reporting job full table scans slowed ledger-db' (2025-05-22, tied to settlement-service, match_score 4); HIST-109 token validation regression with 401 invalid_token (2025-07-11); HIST-114 ledger-db disk full from retained WAL (2025-04-18, write failures).

Several matched precedents are cases where the failure was silent at the HTTP layer or caused by shared components: HIST-109 (auth library upgrade producing 401 invalid_token, found only via token validation), HIST-115 'connection pool misconfiguration' with 'request timed out'/'pool exhausted' (config_change), HIST-112 settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment (consumer lag growing, settlements stuck), HIST-104 Kafka broker rebalance lag.
